claims.statement: The bridge reads stdin one byte at a time on a reader thread, queues each completed line as a Line event, and queues an Oversized event for a line over the cap, discarding input through the next newline.
AgentLineReader strips one trailing CR before the LF and applies the 1 MiB cap (kAgentMaxLineBytes, 1 << 20) to the line without that CR, reporting Oversized for a longer line.
An oversized stdio line produces one JSON-RPC Invalid Request error with a null id, and its content is not parsed.

McpSession accepts protocol 2026-07-28 per request through the io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion _meta key, rejects other modern versions with -32022, and requires initialize before requests without modern _meta (-32600); initialize selects 2025-06-18 or 2025-11-25, defaulting to 2025-11-25.

GuiLink connects lazily when no channel is open: it reads the endpoint file, opens a loopback connection within the 3 s connect timeout, sends hello with the bridge token, protocol, and client identity within the 5 s hello timeout, and keeps the link only when the GUI token matches the endpoint file and the catalog version equals the bridge's.

GuiLink call waits up to the 120 s call timeout for the reply, drops its channel after a transport failure or a JSON-RPC error reply, and reports SimulatorUnavailable with a fixed reachability message when the GUI cannot be reached.

AgentListener accepts IPv4 loopback peers only. AgentServer handles one active client and gives one newcomer a 100 ms replacement grace; it admits that newcomer if the active client closes, otherwise sends BUSY and closes it. A second newcomer during the grace receives BUSY immediately. A client that does not complete hello within the configured timeout (5 s by default) is closed.
The server answers a hello whose catalog_version differs with VERSION_MISMATCH and otherwise replies with the GUI token and the current epoch.
The listener thread only frames sockets and validates envelopes, queueing calls under a mutex; pump on the UI thread alone checks dialog state and invokes the executor.

RFSimulatorApp::update_dsp calls AgentServer::pump before the circuit-runtime update; within a pump, calls run in FIFO order, dialog state is checked before each call, at least one call completes unless the head is parked, and the 8 ms pump_budget is checked only after a call completes.

While a dialog is open the pump parks the queue; the park clock starts when the pump first sees the dialog and resets when it sees none, and the head call receives BUSY with the dialog message once the dialog has stayed open longer than park_timeout (30 s).
Exceptions from the dialog-state query and from the executor become INTERNAL results instead of unwinding the pump, and completion handlers run after the pump releases its lock.

AgentApi::execute routes by tool name through an if-chain of ten branches; an unknown name returns InvalidArgument with the current epoch, AgentArgumentError and other exceptions are returned as error results, and an unexpected exception becomes INTERNAL.
A failed tool result has is_error true and structured {epoch, error:{code, message}}, with hint, op_index, and details present only when set and epoch null when unknown.

circuit_edit requires an epoch equal to the current epoch and between 1 and 64 ops; a stale epoch returns STALE_EPOCH with details.epoch, details.cause when a replacement was recorded, and details.undone after a revert.
receiver_measure checks its epoch before any other argument, so a stale call reports STALE_EPOCH even when its other arguments are invalid.

circuit_edit opens an AppAgentHost checkpoint before operations. Its finish step discards the checkpoint when every applied entry is unchanged; otherwise it commits the summary and places added components. A RESTORE_FAILED error commits even an empty checkpoint. An unchanged move returns applied[].unchanged true, and a batch of only unchanged moves leaves project revision and checkpoint history unchanged.

On the first failing op circuit_edit stops, returns op_index, and reports the applied prefix in structured.applied, which stays committed; a success returns epoch, revision, applied, and refs, where refs name call-local refs.
AppAgentHost keeps the newest 20 committed checkpoints, and removeCheckpointsFrom(id) drops checkpoints at or after id and returns their summaries oldest-first.
The API keeps the undone summaries from a revert through noteProjectReplaced and reports them in the details of the next stale circuit_edit call.
receiver_measure and data_file_read begin no checkpoint, call no EditorCommands, and write no file.
receiver_measure rejects non-finite request numbers as InvalidArgument and encodes each series point through agentNumber, so the NaN the engine uses for an unavailable point becomes JSON null.
data_file_read reports magnitude_dB through agentNumber, so a zero-magnitude sample becomes JSON null, and max_points defaults to 201 within the range 2 to 401.

Each reply line is capped at 1 MiB and written with a 5 s timeout; a tool result over the cap is replaced by an INTERNAL error with the current epoch, and flushOutbox honours a close_connection flag on outbox entries.
receiver_measure runs one bounded update of an API-owned engine per call and returns in_progress, so callers repeat the call while in_progress is true.
test_agent_api, test_agent_server, test_mcp_bridge, and test_agent_app are registered as standalone CTest targets in tests/CMakeLists.txt.
Real-client interoperability, minimized-window behavior, and server-restart persistence are manual acceptance steps, not automated tests.

circuit_get exposes each component's current position in editor-space coordinates, including canvas pan, through the v1 catalog's optional position output field. circuit_edit moves only components that predate the batch with an absolute editor-space position. Pan-scaled float comparisons report a move as unchanged when stored coordinates do not change.
